answer: An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the juniper index resolves every citation against the anchor checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the onyx audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 200 aliases hence pays the authoring cost 200 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 9 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
